contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage

Badges are used to indicate a notification, item count, or other information relating to a navigation destination. They are placed on the ending edge of icons, typically within other components.

There are two variants:

  1. Small badge

  2. Large badge

contentChunks.footer: Navigation bar with four badges
contentChunks.altText: Diagram of 4 badges in different configurations on a navigation bar's destination icons.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
A small badge is a simple circle, used to indicate an unread notification.  

A large badge contains label text communicating item count information.

contentChunks.footer: Small badge
contentChunks.altText: A small badge is a circle with no characters.

contentChunks.footer: Large badge
contentChunks.altText: A large badge holds 4 characters and expands its container's width but not height.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
With other components

Badges are most commonly used within other components, such as navigation bar, navigation rail, app bars, and tabs.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Container

There are two container options for the badge: 

  • Small badge with no text

  • Large badge with text

contentChunks.footer: A small badge uses only shape to indicate a status change or new notification
contentChunks.altText: A small badge on a navigation item.

contentChunks.footer: A large badge displays a number within a container to indicate a quantifiable status change related to a destination
contentChunks.altText: Number 10 displayed within large badge on a navigation item.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Badge containers are anchored inside the icon bounding box. As the number count increases for large badges, their width expands, but keeps the same placement.

Badges use a color intended to stand out against labels, icons, and navigation elements. Use the default color mapping to avoid color conflict issues.

contentChunks.footer: Change the position of the badge for right-to-left languages
contentChunks.altText: Small and large badges on the left side of 2 navigation items in a right-to-left language.

contentChunks.footer: Badges have fixed positions. Don’t change the position of the badge arbitrarily or place the badge over the icon.
contentChunks.altText: Small and large badges at random positions on 3 icon buttons on a navigation rail.

contentChunks.footer: Use the default badge color
contentChunks.altText: Small and large badges in default red color on 3 navigation items.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid using custom color roles for the badge container and label text. If custom roles are necessary, make sure they have contrast of at least 3:1.
contentChunks.altText: Small and large badges in custom colors on 3 navigation items.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Label text

Label large badges with counts or a status. The maximum number of characters within large badge label text is four, including a + to indicate more.

contentChunks.footer: Large badges with one to four characters
contentChunks.altText: 4 icons with increasing number badges. The badges represent quantities, using a "+" symbol for quantities over 999.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Use the recommended maximum character count to ensure labels don’t extend beyond the badge container.

contentChunks.footer: Truncate badge labels as needed
contentChunks.altText: 4-digit numbers condensed to a 3-digit badge with "+" to fit the badge container's width.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t let the badge get cut off or collide with another element
contentChunks.altText: 4-digit and 5-digit number badges on navigation items exceed the badge container's width and get cut off at the edge.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Placement

contentChunks.footer: Use a large badge to show count information when visual collisions aren’t an issue, such as in a navigation rail
contentChunks.altText: Large badge to the right of a navigation rail item.

contentChunks.footer: Use a small badge when spaces are tightly constrained, such as app bars. Small badges won’t run into the edge of the screen.
contentChunks.altText: Small badge on an icon button in an app bar.

contentChunks.footer: When an icon with a badge is followed by text or another element, place a large badge at the trailing edge
contentChunks.altText: Large badge placed at the end of a tab.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid using a large badge when it might overlap with a trailing element. Either place it at the trailing edge or use a small badge instead.
contentChunks.altText: Large badge overlapping the icon and text in a tab.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Use cases

People should be able to use assistive technology to:

  • Understand the dynamic information conveyed in badges, such as counts or labels
  • Address badge announcements by selecting corresponding navigation destinations
Interaction & style

Badges are most commonly used within other components, such as navigation bar, navigation rail, app bars, and tabs.

When a badge is used to indicate an unread notification, the badge gets hidden once it's selected.

contentChunks.altText: An animation of a badge disappearing once it's tapped.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Visual indicators
Badges use a color intended to stand out against labels, icons, and navigation elements. Use the default color mapping to avoid color conflict issues.

contentChunks.footer: Badges must use default color with at least 3:1 contrast
contentChunks.altText: Diagram of large and small badges showing that they need to pass 3 to 1 contrast.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid using custom color roles for the badge container and label text. If custom roles are necessary, make sure they have contrast of at least 3:1.
contentChunks.altText: Diagram of large and small badges not passing 3 to 1 contrast.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Labeling elements

The accessibility label for a badge item will be read after its navigation destination. Any numerical badges will have their number read, while non-counting badges will simply announce New notification.

contentChunks.footer: Numerical badges will have their number read
contentChunks.altText: Navigation bar highlighting numerical badge.

contentChunks.footer: Non-counting badges will simply announce New notification
